brief: MUFG forecasts September payrolls to grow 90k, above the Bloomberg median of 85k and the 71k three-month average, because leisure & hospitality and local-government hiring normalizes after August's rebound while healthcare, professional & business services, construction and manufacturing hold steady, keeping growth in a 70-110k range. Unemployment is forecast to hold at 4.1%, matching consensus: a drop in labor-force participation among workers 55 and over (more retirements) offsets gains in prime-age (25-54) participation, though normal-volatility job losses could push it to 4.2%. The Chicago Fed Nowcast sees 4.1% as most likely, with equal odds of 4.0% or 4.2%. MUFG's framing is that this print matters less for Fed pricing at the front end than for forward growth expectations priced further out the curve, so a stable-narrative consensus print is unlikely to move markets much, though current momentum could extend into Friday with a front-end rally on fading October hike odds. A weaker-than-expected report should trigger a bull flattener as the 10Y rallies on a weaker growth outlook; an especially strong report should trigger a bear steepener, driven more by the growth read than by added Fed hikes being priced in.
